prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic. EMPTY SET PLATE, ABSOLUTELY NO PEOPLE AND NO ANIMALS IN THIS IMAGE. This is the EXACT SAME SHED INTERIOR as the attached plate, from the SAME CAMERA, with the SAME walls, the SAME four-pane window, the SAME workbench, the SAME doorway at the far left with green grass beyond it, the SAME shelves and pegboard and the SAME bare bulb. Match that room exactly. THE ONE CHANGE: a LINE OF FIVE SMALL HAND-MADE MACHINES now stands in a row ALONG THE BENCH, arranged in process order running from the NEAR RIGHT END OF THE BENCH toward the DOORWAY AT THE FAR LEFT. In order they are: FIRST, nearest the viewer, a small wooden gadget with two soft felt-covered fingers that touch a sheet of paper; SECOND, a simple guillotine-style paper cutter with a wooden handle; THIRD, a CLEAR OPEN EMPTY STRETCH OF BENCH with nothing on it at all, which is where the folding happens by hand; FOURTH, a small hardwood roller on a frame for pressing creases; and LAST, at the far left end beside the doorway, a hand-made launcher: a pale wooden upright post C-clamped to the bench end carrying a hinged wooden arm with a visible coiled steel spring at its pivot and a cork-and-wire cradle at its tip. Every one of the five is plainly built by children out of scrap wood, tin and wire, mismatched and a little crooked. NONE of them has a motor, wires, electronics, dials, gauges, screens or any glow. The room stays SMALL, WOODEN, CLUTTERED AND WARM and NEVER becomes a laboratory, a factory floor or a maker-space. RENDER ONE SINGLE MOMENT IN TIME: one view of one room, never a before-and-after, never a split panel, never two versions side by side. ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
